notes: Same WAF block as rancho-muscupiabe; zero PDF pages read. THIS IS THE ONE SUBSTANTIVE FINDING IN MY SIX and it is exactly the trap the brief warned about: an unflagged record whose bare 'Confirmed' hides a partial rejection, with the final decree sitting in an unread volume of a MULTI-VOLUME case - here four volumes, A through D, not two. Hoffman 1862 also reads 'confirmed' with no qualifier, which is why the record came through unflagged: Hoffman's table was printed in 1862 and the 1859 Supreme Court rejection of the sobrante is simply not representable in his disposition column, so Hoffman-agreement is NOT evidence of a clean record for any grant with a split disposition. That is a systematic blind spot in the flagging, not a one-off. Bowman also states 'The patent is found in this case, 319 ND, but without the surveyor's plat', so patent_to / patent_date / glo_patent_no become gradeable from the file itself on a real read - unusual, and worth doing. Acreage breakdown given: Yuba 25,375.55, Sutter 14,584.74, Sacramento 8,879.01 (sums to 48,839.30, matching the register). OAI 'Associated Case Numbers: Toma 97, Expediente 250, Docket 92, 319 ND, GLO 20' - Docket 92 matches hoffman_1862.commission_no 92. Bowman adds a naming detail worth carrying: 'In the titulo the name is written Nueva Elvecia; and on the traced diseno in the case it is written Nueva Helvecia.' DUPLICATE ROW: this record and 'rancho-new-helvetia-1' are identical in every claimed field, in scan_record_url and in hoffman_1862 - see that record's notes.
